findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A repository requires a Jenkins build that GitHub shows as started through a pending commit status, after its GitHub Actions jobs have finished.
The Done-when item is: Close and merge keep waiting while GitHub shows a required check running, up to the same 90-minute limit land uses; when they stop at a limit they say which limit and that the checks are still running.
The coordinator's note considered check runs, but `checks.py:495-496` also accepts commit statuses. A provider can report a started build using a [pending status](https://issues.jenkins.io/browse/JENKINS-22157). Because `running` at line 124 only examines check runs, this branch keeps the ten-minute deadline for that build and stops without naming the limit, even though `_pending` describes it as still running.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - Running Forge's configured test suite after this change.
For an in-progress check with `FORGE_CHECKS_WAIT` set, this branch prepends the no-progress limit to the refusal. `tests/test_close.py:355-358,492-502` still requires the old exact message with the zero override, and `tests/test_land_waits_for_check_progress.py:139-146` requires the old message and excludes the new prefix with the 60-second override. Both tests therefore fail by inspection; their expectations need to reflect the new limit message.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A coordinator runs standalone merge, or Forge's generated workflow runs a long test group.
The named proof invokes only `close`; the existing merge revalidation test at `tests/test_land_waits_for_check_progress.py:150-171` invokes `land`, which sets `wait_for_progress=True` in `src/forge/land.py:53`. A regression limited to standalone `merge` can pass both. The new fixture also uses a running check named `tests`, while `.github/workflows/forge.yml:41-44,91-98` runs `test group ...` before the required `tests` aggregate exists, so an implementation that waits only for the named check can pass while the reported test-group case fails. Finally, the limit assertion checks only printed words, not elapsed time or the check name, and the zero-override assertion also passes if the override is ignored and the command eventually times out at 90 minutes.

why: Close and merge stop waiting after 10 minutes while the pull request's test groups are still running, so on repos with 30-minute test groups the coordinator reruns close and merge several times per change (#1500)
